page: Google Cloud Platform c2-standard-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this server is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor features 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 24 MB of L3 cache. It includes advanced instruction set extensions such as AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, and AVX-512 Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI), alongside AES cryptography acceleration and BMI2, ADX, and FMA integer manipulation flags. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves average performance in single-core metrics, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1572.39 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1309.0. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression (26.8 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (10.09 GB/sec) also register in the average tier. However, multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks fall into the weak or poor categories. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is rated weak at 4147.67, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 2855.0. Memory bandwidth is limited, with large-block read and write speeds measuring 28.26 GB/sec and 24.11 GB/sec respectively, which are categorized as weak.

Given its hardware profile, the c2-standard-4 offers a dedicated compute resource allocation that avoids the CPU-sharing overhead of burstable instances, providing predictable single-threaded execution. However, its resource density and weak multi-core scaling present a tradeoff for highly parallelized workloads. It is best suited for workloads that benefit from high clock speeds and single-core performance rather than massive parallelization or high memory bandwidth. Suitable applications include lightweight web serving, single-threaded data processing, basic text processing, and small-scale LLM text generation using compact models.
